(Amruthahalli Police) Against The Petitioner
Herein, For The Alleged Offences P/U/Sec.498A R/W 34
Of Ipc And Section 3 And 4 Of D.P. Act In
C.C.No.13473/2017 On The File Of C.M.M., Bengaluru,
For The Reasons Stated Herein Above.

This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioners have challenged the prosecution initiated against them in C.C.No.13473/2017 pending trial before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru (Henceforth to be referred as Trial Court) for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Section 498-A of IPC.
2.
The respondent No.2 lodged a complaint with respondent No.1 on 29.09.2016 accusing the petitioners of demanding dowry and also harassing and treating her cruelty.
She also alleged that both the petitioners had threatened her and her family members.

Based on such complaint,
respondent No.1 registered Crime No.147/2016 for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Respondent No.1 took up investigation and thereafter, filed a charge sheet against the petitioners for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Section 498A of IPC.
The Trial Court took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued process, which is challenged in this petition.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that respondent No.2 had initiated proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 in Criminal Miscellaneous No.217/2012 before the jurisdictional Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court No.5 at Bengaluru.

sentences.text: A sum of Rs.9,00,000/- was to be paid at the time of filing petition for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.
The learned counsel submits that the petition for dissolution of marriage was filed in M.C.No.1624/2019 and a sum of Rs.9,00,000/- was paid before the Court.

Consequent to which,
the Court passed an order dissolving the marriage between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2.
He submits that respondent No.2 had conceded that C.C.No.13473/2017 can also be closed by filing appropriate petition before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 does not dispute the above and submits that respondent No.2 is presently residing in the United State of America.

In view of the fact that the parties have settled the dispute and in view of the fact that petitioner No.1 has paid a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- and the relationship between petitioner No.1 and respondent No2 is dissolved, no further steps need to be taken to continue the prosecution against the petitioners.
In that view of the matter, this petition is allowed.

The prosecution of the petitioners in C.C.No.13473/2017 on the file of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Section 498-A of IPC is quashed.
